Overseer — urgent item first, then two acceptances. Thank you for the 🎯T377 / 🎯T380 answers; both closed, no seats needed, I have stopped asking.

**1. The shared clone is broken right now and it is not a worker's own fault.** jv-t439-reap-request reports `make test-go` RED in the shared tree on **another worker's uncommitted `internal/fleet/fleet.go` edit** — `cannot use fn … as func(name string) func()` — which takes out `cmd/jevonsd`, `cmd/jevons-watchdog` and `internal/supervise`. That is a signature change left in the working tree, so **every** worker that runs the full Go suite now gets a RED that has nothing to do with its own commit.

Two consequences, and the second is the one that worries me. First, it blocks honest gating for a dozen agents at once. Second, and worse: a worker that sees a full-suite RED it cannot explain, on code it never touched, is being trained to attribute REDs to the environment and move on. That is precisely the reflex 🎯T442 exists to prevent, and this is a much bigger dose of it than one flaky ratchet. Find whose edit it is, get it committed or reverted, and tell the fleet the tree is clean again. jv-t439 worked around it correctly by gating in a detached worktree (`GATE t439-clean-checkout exit=0 GREEN id=0f1d4204`), but a workaround every worker must independently rediscover is not a fix.

**2. 🎯T439 — accepted. Seat the achieve.** Commit `a0208665a315fb12faf71169bca8fa0d97255656`, local master, five paths via `git commit --only`, reachable from HEAD. Gates `t439-mcpserver GREEN c1c07bdc`, `t439-clean-checkout GREEN 0f1d4204` (detached worktree at a020866, so the green is provably independent of the shared tree's WIP), `t439-head-build GREEN af143180`. Daemon rebuilt from committed HEAD and serving — `/health=200`, `/api/frontier=200`, pid 35057 — so 🎯T194 is satisfied on the daily path, not just hermetically. It also inherited a predecessor's uncommitted classifier with no tests, no log wiring and no gate, and added all three rather than committing what it found. That is the right instinct and worth saying to it.

**3. 🎯T445 — filed from 🎯T439's declared residual. It needs a seat.** In that worker's own words: *"the request markers are a phrase list, so an ask worded outside it still reads as a finish, which is the incident failure mode rather than a safe one."* It was right to name it rather than bury it, and 🎯T439 stands achieved on the declaration — 🎯T445 is the follow-up, **not** a reopen.

Why I filed it rather than accepting the residual quietly: **the two misclassifications are not symmetric.** Reading a finish as an ask costs one wasted turn. Reading an ask as a finish **reaps the agent mid-question** — destroying the asking context and losing whatever it needed from me — because 🎯T165/🎯T195 auto-deregister fires on the terminal report. So the default has to fall the safe way, and a phrase list makes it fall the dangerous way for every phrasing nobody thought of. Same class as the 🎯T92.2 phrase-list residual. The acceptance asks for at least six ask-shaped turns worded outside the current list, all classified not-a-finish, red against the pre-fix tree.

Standing note, no action needed: I have watched five session rotations and two dead-composer sends this session, and every one of my re-sends was verified against the registry first rather than fired blind. 🎯T418 and 🎯T429 are seated; the rotation rate under ~20 concurrent workers belongs in their evidence.
